memory_update.text: SPSC is the highest-priority underfollowed candidate for retail supplier connectivity networks because it is the most direct public pure-play found in this pass.
DSGX should remain in the universe as a broader logistics/B2B connectivity platform with large connected-party scale; later layers need to isolate retail/wholesale EDI contribution.
OTEX is a reference/context name for business networks and EDI scale, but purity is lower because Business Network is embedded in a broader enterprise software portfolio.
MANH is a second-order hypothesis rather than a direct EDI-network candidate; keep only if supplier enablement/trading-partner workflows prove material to customer lock-in.

Private competitors such as TrueCommerce and Cleo appear important to the node but are not US-listed pure-play candidates; they should be used as competitive benchmarks in later diligence rather than public-market candidates.

node: Retail supplier connectivity, EDI/API networks, order/invoice compliance, and trading-partner maps
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the retail supplier connectivity node. The cleanest underfollowed pure-play found is SPS Commerce, whose public filings describe a global supply-chain network, 100 consecutive quarters of revenue growth, and recurring-revenue customers. Descartes and OpenText are larger network/platform comparables with broad B2B/EDI trading-partner networks, but retail-supplier exposure is less pure because both span logistics, enterprise information management, or broader integration markets. Manhattan Associates is included as a second-order infrastructure hypothesis: it is not primarily an EDI network, but its retail supply-chain, order-management, warehouse, transportation, and supplier-enablement footprint may sit adjacent to the same retailer-specific compliance maps and workflows.
